headline: Treasury's bond rescue lifts risk appetite after a rough tech stretch
body: Equities enter today's session trying to shake off three straight down days driven less by earnings than by the bond market: the 30-year Treasury yield touched roughly 5.33%, its highest since 2007, and semiconductor stocks bore the brunt, with Nvidia, Micron, and AMD all down sharply as chipmakers led a Nasdaq slide. Relief came from an unusual source -- Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the government would at least double its buybacks of longer-dated debt, and yields responded immediately, with the 10-year falling to about 4.65% and the 30-year easing to roughly 5.20%. Futures flipped from broadly negative to closer to flat, with the Nasdaq-100 modestly higher and the Dow essentially unchanged -- a tentative, yield-led bounce rather than a broad conviction rally.

Risk appetite showed up most visibly in crypto: bitcoin climbed more than 10% over two sessions to top $71,000, its strongest level since early June, with over $1 billion in short positions liquidated in under an hour and ether pushing above $2,300 alongside it -- a move traders are tying to the same falling-yield backdrop plus renewed White House pressure for crypto-friendly legislation. Geopolitical headlines, including a newly announced US economic campaign aimed at isolating Iran, are running in the background without yet reshaping the tape. Retail chatter on Reddit and StockTwits doesn't show a clear single-name obsession today, so this read leans more on price action and the yield story than on social sentiment.
